h1: The 6 Best Toaster Ovens That Hold 9 Slices of Toast, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 large toaster ovens in the 9-slice class compared on capacity, air fry and convection, French doors and price bracket.
summary: The Emeril Lagasse 26QT French door oven is the best balance of capacity, air fry and price for a household that wants one big toaster oven. The Gourmia 37 Qt is the pick if you cook for a crowd, the Elite Gourmet ETO2530M is the cheapest way into French doors, and the Typhur Sync adds a wireless meat probe.
intro: A slice count on a toaster oven box is a marketing number, not a measurement. Brands calculate it by lining slices edge to edge on the rack, which is more than you will ever want to do with real bread, and it says nothing about whether a 12 inch pizza or a 9 by 13 inch pan fits. The honest way to read a 9-slice claim is as a size class, around 25 to 35 liters, and then to check what the oven can do inside that space.

This ranking is built around that idea. We reviewed six large toaster ovens from their listings and spec sheets, comparing capacity in quarts and liters, whether they air fry or convection bake, door style, wattage where listed, and price bracket. Listings rarely state interior dimensions, so we flag where you should check them before buying.

products.name: Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door Multi-Function Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A 26 quart French door oven that air fries, with the best mix of size and price.
products.description:
The Emeril Lagasse oven has a 26 quart capacity, French doors and an air fry function in a multi-function design. It is priced in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It earns the first slot because 26 quarts, roughly 25 liters, sits at the heart of the 9-slice class: big enough for a 12 inch pizza or a family-size tray of wings, but still short enough to fit under most kitchen cabinets. The French doors open together with one pull, which matters more than it sounds when the shelf is full of hot food. Against the Gourmia below it, you give up capacity but gain a more manageable footprint.

Buy it if you want one oven that can replace a toaster, a small air fryer and a countertop baker. The caveat is that the listing does not give wattage or interior dimensions.
pros: 26 quart size sits in the sweet spot
French doors open in one motion
Air fry built into the oven
products.idealFor: Families who want one oven to replace several gadgets.
products.skipIf: You need to roast a large turkey breast.

products.name: Gourmia French Door Air Fryer Oven - 37 Qt Large Capacity Convection
products.verdict: A 37 quart French door convection air fryer for cooking on a family scale.
products.description:
The Gourmia is a 37 quart, about 35 liter, French door oven with convection and air fry in the $100 to $200 range.

It takes second place because capacity is its biggest argument. The extra quarts mean you can cook on two racks at once without crowding, and a convection fan moves hot air so the top and bottom racks brown more evenly. Compared with the Emeril, it pushes past the usual 9-slice envelope, so it needs more counter space and takes longer to preheat.

It is the right choice for a large household or someone who entertains and wants to bake and air fry in volume. The honest tradeoff is bulk: measure the counter and the cabinet clearance first.
cons: Takes a lot of counter room
Slower to preheat a big cavity
products.skipIf: Your counter or cabinet clearance is tight.

products.name: Elite Gourmet ETO2530M Double French Door Oven
products.verdict: A 25 liter double French door oven in the $50 to $100 bracket, without air fry.
products.description:
The ETO2530M is a 25 liter oven with double French doors, in the $50 to $100 bracket. It does not list air fry, so it works as a conventional toaster oven.

It earns the third slot because it is the cheapest way into the 9-slice class and gives you the French door convenience. It loses to the Emeril on cooking range since there is no air fry mode, and the capacity is slightly smaller. The listing does not state whether it has convection, so check before assuming even browning.

Pick it if toast, bagels and reheating are your main uses. Skip it if you want crispy air-fried food.
pros: French doors in a mid-size oven
products.idealFor: Toast, bagels and reheating for a small family.

products.name: Beelicious 32QT Extra Large Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 32 quart, 1800W air fryer oven with a clearly stated power rating.
products.description:
The Beelicious is a 32 quart air fryer oven with 1800W of power, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It earns the fourth slot because the wattage is a rare piece of transparent data. 1800W is near the top of what a standard 15 amp household circuit supports, so it should heat quickly, though it also means you should not share the outlet with a kettle. Against the Emeril, it offers a bigger cavity but fewer features that the listing highlights, such as door style.

It makes sense for buyers who want a lot of air fry capacity. The caveat is that brand reputation and long-term support are unproven.
products.idealFor: Air fry fans who want a big, powerful oven.

products.name: Typhur Sync Oven with Smart Wireless Meat Thermometer Probe
products.verdict: An air fry oven bundled with a wireless meat thermometer for hands-off roasting.
products.description:
The Typhur Sync is an air fry oven that ships with a smart wireless meat thermometer probe, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It earns the fifth slot because the probe is its identity. A wireless probe lets you roast chicken, pork or steak to a target internal temperature without opening the door, which is the single best way to avoid overcooked meat. The listing does not give capacity, so you must verify it fits your pan sizes. Against the models above, you pay for smart features rather than raw volume.

Buy it if you roast meat often and want accuracy. Skip it if you mostly make toast.
pros: Takes the guesswork out of roasts
products.idealFor: Home cooks who roast meat and want precise doneness.

products.name: Nuwave Bravo XL Pro Air Fryer Toaster Oven w/Grill Combo
products.verdict: An air fry toaster oven with a grill function, but in the highest price bracket here.
products.description:
The Nuwave Bravo XL Pro combines air frying with a grill function in a toaster oven, in the $200 to $500 bracket.

It sits at the bottom because it costs more than anything else in this ranking while the listing provides little capacity detail. A grill function gives better browning on top of steaks and sausages, which helps if you cook meat often. Against the Emeril, you pay roughly double for a different set of features, not a bigger oven.

Choose it if the grill mode appeals to you and you accept the price. Otherwise the Emeril or Gourmia offers more space for less.
pros: Air fry in the same unit
products.idealFor: Meat lovers who want top-down grilling.
products.skipIf: Value and capacity are your priorities.

whatMatters.detail: A slice count depends on how bread is laid on the rack. Capacity in quarts or liters is a better measure: 25 L is about 26 quarts. Look for interior width, depth and height on the listing, and check them against the pan or pizza you plan to use.

A convection fan circulates hot air, which cuts cooking time and evens out browning, while air fry mode adds a stronger fan and a wire basket. Both help food crisp. Listings that mention only a toaster function probably have no fan at all.

French doors open both sides with one pull and save you from reaching over a hot, flat drop-down door. They take space on each side when open, so check clearance. Look at how the door seals and whether it has a handle that stays cool.

A 1500 to 1800W oven draws most of a 15 amp circuit, so do not run it alongside another high-draw appliance. Higher wattage preheats faster. If a listing omits power, assume it sits in the usual range and check the label.

A removable crumb tray and a non-stick interior make a toaster oven bearable to keep clean. Look for those features by name. Air fry baskets and racks that go in the dishwasher are another real convenience.

faq.a: On the 26 quart Emeril and larger ovens, usually yes, since pizza fits in roughly the 25 liter class. Check the listed interior width for the Elite Gourmet before you rely on it.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake when buying a large toaster oven?
faq.a: Choosing by slice count. Two ovens that both claim 9 slices can differ in height and depth by several inches, so compare capacity and interior dimensions.

faq.q: Is air fry worth paying extra for?
faq.a: If you cook wings, fries or reheat leftovers, yes, since the fan crisps in minutes. For toast alone, the Elite Gourmet is cheaper and does the same job.

faq.q: How much counter space do I need?
faq.a: Leave several inches at the back and sides for airflow, plus the door swing for French models. The 37 quart Gourmia needs notably more space than the 25 L Elite Gourmet.

faq.q: How do I keep one clean?
faq.a: Empty the crumb tray after heavy toasting, wipe the interior when cool, and wash racks and baskets by hand or in the dishwasher where the manual allows. Never let grease build up on the elements.

faq.q: Can I run one on an extension cord?
faq.a: Avoid it. Ovens draw a lot of current, and a thin cord can overheat. Plug directly into a wall outlet, ideally not shared with another high-power appliance.

finalTake: The Emeril Lagasse 26QT is the best large toaster oven for most households, balancing capacity, French doors and air fry. The Gourmia 37 Qt is the choice for big families, and the Elite Gourmet ETO2530M is the cheapest way to get the 9-slice class. Measure your counter and check the interior dimensions before you buy.
